entries.title: Disable the startup-apps notification task
entries.description: Disables the Application Experience StartupAppTask, which scans your startup entries and raises the 'you have too many startup apps' notification.
entries.rationale: The task exists only to surface a startup-app toast. Disabling it removes a small logon-time scan and the notification; the startup apps themselves are unaffected.
sideEffects: You no longer receive the 'you have too many startup apps' notification.

entries.title: Disable Windows Maps background tasks
entries.description: Disables the Windows Maps toast task (MapsToastTask) and the offline-map update task (MapsUpdateTask).
entries.rationale: Windows Maps is deprecated; these tasks only show Maps toasts and download offline-map updates in the background. Disabling them stops that periodic download and notification work.
sideEffects: Offline maps in the Windows Maps app no longer update automatically.
Windows Maps is a deprecated app.

entries.title: Disable the Xbox cloud game-save sync task
entries.description: Disables XblGameSaveTask, which syncs Xbox Live cloud saves for supported titles in the background.
entries.rationale: On PCs that do not play Xbox Live titles this task is idle background work. Gamers who rely on cloud saves should leave it enabled, so this is a Strict, opt-in change.
sideEffects: Xbox Live cloud saves for supported titles stop syncing from this device.
Gamers who use Xbox cloud saves should keep this task enabled.

entries.title: Disable the speech-model download task
entries.description: Disables SpeechModelDownload, which downloads and updates voice-typing and Narrator speech models in the background.
entries.rationale: If you do not use voice typing or Narrator, this task is background download work you can stop. Existing speech models keep working; only automatic updates stop.
sideEffects: Voice typing and Narrator speech models no longer update automatically.

entries.title: Disable the recommended-troubleshooting tasks
entries.description: Disables the Diagnosis Scheduled and RecommendedTroubleshootingScanner tasks that scan for and suggest automatic troubleshooters.
entries.rationale: These tasks periodically check for recommended troubleshooters. Disabling them stops that background scan; you can still run troubleshooters manually from Settings.
sideEffects: Windows no longer scans for or offers automatic 'recommended' troubleshooters. Manual troubleshooters in Settings still work.

entries.title: Disable the Windows Backup app-inventory task
entries.description: Disables MareBackup, the Application Experience task that inventories installed Win32 apps for the Windows Backup app-list restore feature.
entries.rationale: The task periodically catalogues installed desktop apps so Windows Backup can restore the list on a new PC. If you do not use Windows Backup app restore, this is background disk work you can stop.
sideEffects: Windows Backup can no longer restore your list of installed Win32 apps to a new PC.

entries.title: Disable the Program Compatibility Assistant patch-DB task
entries.description: Disables PcaPatchDbTask, which updates the Program Compatibility Assistant patch database.
entries.rationale: The task only refreshes the compatibility patch database used to apply shims to older apps. Existing shims still apply; disabling it stops the periodic database update.
sideEffects: The Program Compatibility Assistant patch database stops receiving updates; compatibility fixes already applied continue to work.

entries.title: Disable the Family Safety enforcement tasks
entries.description: Disables the Shell FamilySafetyMonitor and FamilySafetyRefreshTask tasks that enforce Microsoft Family (parental control) limits.
entries.rationale: On a PC with no child accounts these tasks enforce controls that never apply, so they are safe to disable. If any Microsoft Family child account is configured, leave them enabled: disabling them stops screen-time and content limits.
sideEffects: If any Microsoft Family (child) accounts are configured on this PC, their screen-time and content limits stop being enforced.
Only disable when there are no child accounts on this device.

entries.title: Enable Hardware-accelerated GPU Scheduling (HAGS)
entries.description: Sets HwSchMode to 2 to enable Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling, letting the GPU manage its own video-memory scheduling.
entries.rationale: HAGS can slightly reduce scheduling latency and is required by some features such as DLSS 3 frame generation. Windows already enables it by default on supported GPUs (WDDM 2.7+), so the effect is driver-dependent and marginal; it is exposed as an opt-in Gamer tweak. A reboot is required for the change to take effect.
sideEffects: The effect depends on your GPU and driver; on unsupported GPUs the setting has no effect.
Some features such as DLSS 3 frame generation require HAGS to be on.
The registry mechanism is community-documented and not confirmed against a Microsoft doc.

entries.title: Stop Game Bar opening when a controller connects
entries.description: Sets UseNexusForGameBarEnabled to 0 so pressing the Xbox/Nexus button on a controller no longer opens the Xbox Game Bar.
entries.rationale: Stops the Game Bar popup that appears when a controller's Xbox button is pressed. The Game Bar can still be opened manually with Win+G.
sideEffects: The controller's Xbox/Nexus button no longer opens the Game Bar; use Win+G instead.

entries.title: Disable Game DVR for all users (policy)
entries.description: Sets the machine-wide AllowGameDVR policy to 0, turning off Windows game recording and broadcasting for every user on the PC.
entries.rationale: This is the machine-wide policy counterpart to the per-user Game DVR toggle: it enforces Game DVR off for all accounts, removing the background capture pipeline. Game Bar capture (screenshots and clips) is disabled while the policy is set.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Game Recording and Broadcasting\Enables or disables Windows Game Recording and Broadcasting

sideEffects: Game recording and broadcasting is disabled for all users; the Game Bar's capture features are unavailable while the policy is set.
